body.en: *Intellectual* property refers to creations of the human mind, such as inventions, literary and artistic works, designs, symbols, names and images used in business. Intellectual property rights (IPR) are the legal rights given to the creator to prevent others from using the creation without permission for a certain period. IPR encourages innovation by letting creators earn from their work.
body.kn: ಬೌದ್ಧಿಕ ಆಸ್ತಿ ಎಂದರೆ ಮನಸ್ಸಿನ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಗಳು. ಅನುಮತಿಯಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಇತರರು ಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ಬಳಸದಂತೆ ತಡೆಯುವ ಕಾನೂನು ಹಕ್ಕನ್ನು ಬೌದ್ಧಿಕ ಆಸ್ತಿ ಹಕ್ಕು ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Copyright protects literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works, films, sound recordings and computer programs. A trademark is a word, name, symbol or logo that distinguishes one firm's goods from others'. A geographical indication (GI) identifies goods whose quality comes from their place of origin, such as Mysore Silk, Channapatna toys or Darjeeling tea. A patent is granted for an invention that is new, involves an inventive step and is capable of industrial application; in India it lasts 20 years. Design protects the shape, pattern or ornamental features of an article. Plant varieties and semiconductor integrated circuit layout designs are also protected.

problem.en: Which IPR protects each? (a) A new low-cost water purifier invented by a Dharwad engineer. (b) The logo of a Bengaluru coffee chain. (c) A Kannada novel. (d) Udupi Mallige jasmine grown in Udupi.

steps.en: (a) A new, inventive, industrially usable product: patent.
(b) A logo that distinguishes a firm's goods: trademark.
(d) Quality linked to place of origin: geographical indication.

a A new, inventive, industrially usable product: patent.
b A logo that distinguishes a firm's goods: trademark.
c A literary work: copyright.
d Quality linked to place of origin: geographical indication.
So the answer is a Patent, b Trademark, c Copyright, d Geographical indication.

I. Goods whose quality comes from their place of origin, such as Channapatna toys
II. Literary and musical works and computer programs
III. An invention that is new, inventive and industrially applicable
IV. A word, name or logo that distinguishes a firm's goods.
Patents protect inventions, trademarks protect brand names and logos, GIs protect place-linked goods, and copyright protects creative works and software.
